Based on the context provided, the quote "Never trust a woman whose words are too flattering" is attributed to the play **King Lear**.

The text explicitly states: "...like Goneril in this ... might lead to some deadly hanky-panky--I learned it from this play..." and later mentions "Cornwall praises Edmund for his loyalty to his father, as word is that Edgar ..... He warns Lear to never trust women." Cornwall is a character in *King Lear*, and Goneril is his daughter, one of the main antagonists in that play known for her flattery and betrayal of her father.

<answer>King Lear</answer>
